description: Stable row key for each driver snapshot in the mock dataset.
UTC timestamp for the event or driver snapshot.
IANA time zone used to derive local hour and day-of-week.
Local hour derived from timestamp plus time zone.
Local weekday derived from timestamp plus time zone.
Weekend flag derived from local day-of-week.
Driver identifier from the ELD or carrier identity system.
Vehicle or power unit identifier.
Synthetic trip grouping key for analysis across snapshots.
Scenario template used to generate a plausible freight snapshot.
Latitude captured or normalized from the location event.
Longitude captured or normalized from the location event.
Named metro or corridor bucket derived from coordinates.
State or region code derived from coordinates.
Road category such as interstate, urban arterial, or mountain pass.
Road surface condition inferred from weather and corridor.
Posted speed limit attached from map matching or road network data.
Weather bucket joined from historical or live weather data.
Ambient temperature at the event location and time.
Precipitation intensity joined from the weather feed.
Visibility estimate at the event location and time.
Wind speed joined from the weather feed.
Traffic congestion bucket derived from a traffic provider or state feed.
Current HOS duty status such as driving or on-duty not driving.
Vehicle speed from telematics, ECM, or another motion feed.
Current speed minus joined speed limit.
Minutes since the last logged break or off-duty period.
Continuous driving minutes since the last non-driving status.
Minutes remaining before the driver hits the driving limit.
Minutes remaining before the driver hits the on-duty shift limit.
Minutes remaining in the rolling duty cycle window.
Count of hard brake detections in the trailing 24 hours.
Count of harsh acceleration events in the trailing 24 hours.
Count of recent HOS violations used as historical context.
Days since the driver joined the carrier or program.
Number of previously scored trips available for calibration.
True when the driver has fewer than 30 scored trips.
Engine power status from the ELD.
Accumulated engine hours from the ELD or ECM.
Accumulated vehicle miles.
Estimated idle minutes in the trailing window.
Fuel level from telematics or engine data.
Count of active tire pressure alerts.
Maintenance score for brakes on a 0 to 100 scale.
Days overdue for a maintenance interval or inspection.
True when a check-engine condition is active.
True when an ABS fault is active.
Synthetic risk score from 0 to 100 produced for mock experimentation.
Bucketed version of the risk score.
Synthetic target flag indicating an elevated event likelihood within two hours.
Plain-English intervention suggestion tied to the top risk factor.
Dominant explainability reason for the risk score.
Second-most-important explainability reason for the risk score.
